extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (developers/researchers working with graded modules/graded objects)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for the gradedModules.lib procedures in SINGULAR: usage, return values, purpose, assumptions, notes, and worked examples for operations on graded matrices/modules/ideals/mappings.

rubrics_metrics.name: grdeg
rubrics_metrics.description: grdeg(M) — graded object M; Return: intvec of degrees
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: graded degrees of columns (generators) of M, describing the source of M. Assume: M must be a graded object (matrix/module/ideal/mapping). Note: if M has zero cols it should have attrib(M,'degHomog') set. Example usage and illustrative outputs are provided showing how grdeg reports generator degrees for grobj examples and after operations like grsum and grshift (e.g., grdeg(D) -> 1,1,1,1,2,2; grdeg(D10) -> -9,-9,-9,-9,-8,-8). Also demonstrates interplay with grview output.

rubrics_metrics.name: grview
rubrics_metrics.description: grview(M) — graded object M; Return: nothing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: print the degree/grading data about the GRADED matrix/module/ideal/mapping object M. Assume: M must be graded. The documentation gives examples showing formatted 'Graded homomorphism' output (r^a + r(b)^c <- ...), column/row degree listings, and how grview displays results for grobj, grres outputs, and combinations of graded objects (e.g., grview(A), grview(B), grview(D)). Useful for inspecting degree data and understanding subsequent calls (grdeg, grpres, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: grshift
rubrics_metrics.description: grshift(A, d) — graded object A, int d; Return: shifted graded object
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: shift the grading on A by d: A(i) -> A(i+d). Example: grshift(A,6) produces r(6)^3 + r(5) <- r(5)^2 and grdeg/grview reflect shifted degrees. Note: shifting a zero presentation may do nothing and triggers a warning (e.g., shifting '0 <- 0' leaves it unchanged).

rubrics_metrics.name: grzero
rubrics_metrics.description: grzero() — Return: graded object representing S(0)^1
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute presentation of S(0)^1. Examples show grview(grobj(freemodule(0), intvec(0:0), intvec(0:0))) and grview(grzero()) both yield 'Graded homomorphism: 0 <- 0'. Also used in corner-case examples with grshift and other operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: grtwist
rubrics_metrics.description: grtwist(a,d) — int a, d; Return: graded object representing S(d)^a
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute presentation of S(d)^a. Example: grview(grtwist(5,10)) shows 'Graded homomorphism: r(10)^5 <- 0, given by zero (5 x 0) matrix.' Use to create free summands with specified twists.

rubrics_metrics.name: grtwists
rubrics_metrics.description: grtwists(v) — intvec v; Return: graded object representing S(v[1]) + ... + S(v[size(v)])
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute presentation of S(v[1]) + ... + S(v[size(v)]). Examples: grtwists(intvec(-4,1,6)) prints the corresponding graded homomorphism; grtwists(intvec(0:0)) yields '0 <- 0'. Helpful for creating multiple twisted summands at once.

rubrics_metrics.name: grsum
rubrics_metrics.description: grsum(A, B) — graded objects A and B; Return: graded direct sum of input objects
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute the graded direct sum of A and B. Examples illustrate building larger modules by summing grobj/grtwist/grpower outputs; demonstrates how homogeneity and degree vectors combine and how grview/grdeg report the result. Example: module C = grsum(A,B); print(C); homog(C); grview(C).

rubrics_metrics.name: grpower
rubrics_metrics.description: grpower(A, p) — graded object A, int p > 0; Return: graded direct power A^p
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute the graded direct power A^p. Note: the power p must be positive. Examples show doubling/tripling summands (e.g., grpower(A,2), grpower(B,2)) and how the resulting grview/grdeg/betti outputs reflect the powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: grtranspose
rubrics_metrics.description: grtranspose(M) — graded object M; Return: graded object (graded transpose)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: graded transpose of M. Note: no reordering is performed by this procedure. Examples demonstrate round-trips: grtranspose then grsyz then grtranspose again; corner cases include 0 <- 0, * <- 0, and 0 <- * (matrices with zero rows or columns). Output keeps degree data; used in manipulation of presentations and syzygies.

rubrics_metrics.name: grgens
rubrics_metrics.description: grgens(M) — graded object M (map); Return: graded object
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: try compute graded generators of coker(M) and return them as columns of a graded map. Note: presentation of resulting generated submodule may be different to M. Examples show cases where grgens(M) yields the expected diagonal map equal to M, and counterexamples where grgens(A) != A ("Ups :(! != A"). grgens(grzero()) yields '0 <- 0'. Use to extract generator maps for cokernels but be aware of representation differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: grpres
rubrics_metrics.description: grpres(M) — graded object M (submodule gens); Return: graded module (via coker)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: compute graded presentation matrix of submodule generated by columns of M. Examples illustrate using grgroebner/grobj to form A, then performing graded transpose, syzygy computations (grsyz), grtranspose back, grgens, and finally grpres to get presentations; shows how grpres interacts with grview and how degrees are reflected in the resulting presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: grorder
rubrics_metrics.description: grorder(M) — graded object or list M; Return: same as input
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Purpose: reorder/transform graded object or chain complex M into block form. Assume: M must be a graded object or a list of graded objects. Example context includes large examples (surface name, ideal definitions) where grorder is referenced as a procedure for reorganizing graded objects into block-structured presentations.
